checks.detail: ANSWER.md cites CALL-104, not returned by any tool and not in the inputs

items.reasoning: The agent quotes the transcript: 'Just a chirp. Every minute or so', with no continuous alarm. The call dropped before symptoms could be asked about. The agent did not downgrade the case to non-emergency. It kept it urgent and sent an SMS saying that if anyone has a headache, dizziness, sickness or drowsiness, they should leave and call the gas line. It also escalated with a request to 'Phone Priya today to confirm no symptoms'. That serves the purpose of this item.
items.evidence: ANSWER Q1: 'a single chirp about once a minute, no continuous alarm, no reported symptoms'; ESC-106 recommendation to phone tenant to confirm no symptoms

items.reasoning: The agent identified the sealed battery, the 2019-04-02 fit date and the 7-year life (expired April 2026). It said clause 12.8 does not apply and that the landlord is responsible.
items.evidence: 'Clause 12.8 makes the tenant replace batteries, but this battery is sealed and not replaceable, so the unit itself must be replaced by the landlord.'

items.reasoning: The agent created an urgent ticket (JOB-101), sent a landlord approval request (APR-105) and escalated with a 72-hour target. The SMS tells the tenant not to remove the battery. No contractor was booked yet; the agent waited for landlord approval even though the cost is likely within the £300 limit. Even so, the replacement was raised as urgent and pushed forward.
items.evidence: A1 create_ticket severity urgent; A4 SMS 'Please don't remove the battery from the CO alarm'

items.reasoning: The extractor fan was logged as a separate routine ticket.
items.evidence: A2 JOB-102 routine 'Bathroom extractor fan noisy'

items.reasoning: The agent did not call the tenant back itself. It sent an SMS and asked a human to phone.
The SMS says to leave and call 0800 111 999 if anyone has symptoms or the alarm sounds continuously.
items.evidence: 'or the alarm sounds continuously, open windows, leave the flat and call the Gas Emergency line on 0800 111 999'

items.reasoning: The agent noticed the call dropped and followed up by SMS.
items.evidence: MSG-103 'Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped.'

items.reasoning: The agent did not tell the tenant to replace the battery. It identified the sealed, end-of-life unit.
The agent treated the case as urgent, not as an emergency. It separated likely end-of-life from real CO and gave conditional emergency advice.
items.evidence: Severity: urgent; 'escalate to emergency if symptoms or continuous alarm'

items.reasoning: The agent explicitly told the tenant not to remove the battery.
There was no advice to remove or ignore the alarm, and safety caveats were given.

grades.overall_note: The agent judged this well: it kept the case urgent rather than treating it as a gas emergency, identified the sealed end-of-life unit, gave correct safety advice and the gas emergency number by SMS after the call dropped, and logged the extractor fan as a separate routine job. One weakness is that it asked the landlord for approval instead of booking a contractor within the £300 limit.
